column3: A large forested hill park above the Yong River in Nanning, with a pagoda, tropical plants and gardens. It is a green escape from the busy city.
A museum that explores the cultures of Guangxi's many peoples, including the Zhuang, with costumes, bronze drums, and festivals.
A lake park with bridges, islands and gardens in the middle of Nanning, a favorite place for walks and for people to gather in the evening.
The Yong River winds through Nanning and gives the city its short name, Yong. Riverside parks and bridges light up at night.
A wide, many-layered waterfall on the border with Vietnam, among the largest cross-border waterfalls in Asia. Part of it falls in each country.
Hot rice noodles stir-fried with sour bamboo shoots, garlic, chili, pork and fermented black beans, a Nanning favorite. Its name means "old friend noodles".
Rice noodles in a spicy broth of river snails, pickled bamboo, peanuts and chili. Its smell is very strong, but fans love it. It started in Liuzhou and is now sold across China.
A sweet, sour and savory duck stewed with pickled lemons and ginger, and a typical dish of Nanning's tables.
Rice noodles that are pressed fresh from a machine straight into a bowl of broth, soft and slippery.
Guangxi's sunny valleys grow plenty of mangoes, and in summer markets in Nanning sell them by the basketful.
A colorful brocade woven by the Zhuang people, with geometric and flower patterns, used for bags, blankets and clothes.
Bronze drums have been made by southern peoples for over 2,000 years and are used at festivals and as symbols of power.
A river that winds between green karst peaks, so beautiful that its view appears on the 20-yuan banknote. A boat cruise from Guilin to Yangshuo is a classic trip.
A hill by the Li River in Guilin shaped like an elephant dipping its trunk into the water, and the city's best-known landmark.
A big cave near Guilin with colored lights shining on stalactites and stalagmites, which form strange shapes.
A lone peak rising within the old city of the Ming princes. A staircase leads to the top for a view of the city.
Rice terraces that climb the mountainside in curves like a dragon's spine. The Zhuang and Yao villages here have farmed them for centuries.
A quiet, clear river with old bridges and bamboo rafts, among fields and karst hills, calmer than the Li River.
A cave of glittering white rock formations that sparkle like silver under the lights.
Round rice noodles served with braised meat, peanuts and a rich spiced broth, eaten for breakfast in Guilin.
A famous Yangshuo dish of river fish cooked in beer with tomatoes and chili in a pot.
Lipu taro is big and starchy, with a purple pattern, and is used for the famous dish of taro cooked with pork.
A savory tea of fried tea leaves, ginger and garlic, ground and boiled with water, and served with peanuts and crispy snacks.
A soft sweet cake scented with the flowers of the osmanthus. Guilin means "Forest of Osmanthus" and its trees bloom in autumn.
The Red Yao women of Longji grow their hair to remarkable lengths, wash it in rice water and wind it into headdresses.
Yangshuo's lively West Street is a mix of old lanes, cafés, shops and travelers from all over the world.
A hill with a huge round hole in its top, like a full moon seen from a distance. You can climb up to the arch.
An old riverside town with a famous view of rocky peaks and fishermen on bamboo rafts, which appears on the 20-yuan note.
Bamboo rafts carry travelers on slow trips down the river past the peaks, steered with a long pole.
Yangshuo's own style of beer fish is cooked at the table with local beer and fresh river fish.
River snails stuffed with minced pork and herbs and then simmered, a Yangshuo treat that is eaten with a toothpick.
A legendary Zhuang singer who defeated rich rivals in song contests. Her story is told in songs, a film and an outdoor show on the Li River.
The original home of the snail noodle soup. In Liuzhou, locals eat it on every street corner.
A long beach of fine, pale sand on the coast at Beihai, with gentle water, good for walks and for swimming.
A volcanic island off Beihai with black rocks, coral, cliffs and sunsets, and a quiet place with fishing villages.
A mangrove reserve on the coast, where tangled roots shelter crabs, fish and many birds in the shallow water.
Beihai's restaurants serve fresh shrimp, crab and fish, cooked simply to bring out the taste of the sea.
Sandworms are a prized seafood in Beihai, cooked in soup, fried or steamed. They are said to be sweet and tender.
Hepu has been a pearl-producing area for over 2,000 years, and its pearls were once sent to the emperor.
A dark herbal jelly, slightly bitter and eaten with syrup, thought in southern China to cool the body.
Seasoned chicken wrapped in paper and fried in oil, so that the meat stays juicy and fragrant.
A mango from the sunny valley of the Youjiang river, sweet and rich and a famed fruit.
A local breed of duck from Jingxi, known for its tender meat, and often cooked with herbs.
Red paintings of people with raised arms on a cliff above the Zuo River, made over 2,000 years ago by ancestors of the Zhuang. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The main land crossing between China and Vietnam. This old pass has guarded the border for centuries.
Chongzuo is China's biggest sugar-cane area, and the fields stretch for miles around the town.
Rice noodles in a broth with braised pig's feet, soft and rich, a hearty dish of Qinzhou.
Large, plump oysters from the bay at Qinzhou, grilled with garlic or steamed, are a local pride.
Cured and spiced beef, cut into strips and dried. It is chewy and flavorful and a favorite snack.
A herbal drink made in Yulin, brewed from plants and sold in shops to cool the body in the heat.
A small breed of pig from Bama, known for its tender meat. It is often roasted.
A soup of hemp seeds, a staple in Bama, a place known for its long-lived residents.
